title: Cellular imaging of endosome entrapped small gold nanoparticles
author: Kim, Li, et al.

steps.title: Synthesize dodecanethiol‑protected AuNPs
steps.instruction: Prepare 2 nm AuNP‑DT via the Brust–Schiffrin two‑phase method, grow to 4 nm and 6 nm by heat‑induced size evolution, then functionalize by Murray’s place‑exchange method.

substeps.instruction: Use the Brust–Schiffrin two‑phase synthesis to obtain dodecanethiol‑protected AuNPs with a 2 nm core diameter.
Heat 2‑nm AuNP‑DT at a rate of 2 °C/min to 154 °C and hold for 30 min to obtain 4 nm AuNP‑DT; repeat at 165 °C for 30 min to obtain 6 nm AuNP‑DT.
Apply Murray’s place‑exchange method to introduce the desired surface functionality onto the 4‑nm and 6‑nm AuNP‑DT.

steps.title: Characterize AuNP size and surface
steps.instruction: Determine particle size by TEM and DLS, verify surface chemistry by 1H NMR and LDI‑MS, and measure zeta potential.

substeps.instruction: Record transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images and dynamic light scattering (DLS) measurements to assess particle size.
Perform proton nuclear magnetic resonance (¹H NMR) and laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI‑MS) to confirm surface functionalities.
Measure zeta‑potential values using a Malvern Zetasizer Nano ZS instrument.

steps.title: Culture cells and perform AuNP uptake
steps.instruction: Seed HeLa and MCF‑7 cells, incubate, wash, expose to AuNPs at specified concentrations, incubate, wash, and collect for imaging and ICP‑MS.

substeps.instruction: Seed HeLa and MCF‑7 cells into a 24‑well plate at 25,000 cells per well in low‑glucose DMEM supplemented with 10 % FBS and 1 % antibiotic.
Maintain cultures at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere with 5 % CO₂.
After 24 h, wash cells once with PBS.
Add DMEM containing AuNPs: for 4‑nm AuNPs use concentrations of 2.5, 10, 20, 40, and 60 nM; for 6‑nm AuNPs use 0.7, 2.7, 5.5, 10.9, and 16.4 nM.
Include control wells that receive medium only (no AuNPs).
Incubate for 3 h at 37 °C.
Wash cells three times with PBS to remove excess nanoparticles.
Proceed to imaging and/or ICP‑MS quantification.

steps.title: Digest cells and prepare ICP‑MS standards
steps.instruction: Lyse cells with aqua regia, dilute, prepare gold standards containing 5 % aqua regia, run ICP‑MS, and generate a calibration curve.

substeps.instruction: Digest the harvested cells with 0.5 mL fresh aqua regia for 10 min.
Dilute each digested sample to a final volume of 10 mL with deionized water.
Prepare gold standard solutions of 20, 10, 5, 2, 1, 0.5, 0.2, and 0 ppb, each containing 5 % aqua regia.
Measure each standard five times by ICP‑MS using the instrument settings described in the original method.
Construct a calibration curve from the standard measurements and calculate the gold amount taken up by the cells.

steps.title: Acquire confocal reflection images
steps.instruction: Set up the Zeiss 510 inverted CLSM in reflection mode with a 514 nm argon laser and appropriate optics, then capture images at multiple locations.

substeps.instruction: Configure the Zeiss 510 CLSM (inverted) in reflection mode using 63× and 40× oil‑immersion objectives.
Place a drop of immersion oil on each objective lens.
Position the culture dish (coverslip uncovered) on the objective lenses.
Use a 514 nm argon laser (15 mW) reflected by a mirror to illuminate the sample.
Insert a dichroic beam splitter (NT 80/20, Carl Zeiss) for excitation.
Focus the laser to a spot within 1 mm of the sample.
Collect scattered light through a long‑pass 505 nm emission filter.
Adjust focus using differential interference contrast (DIC) as a reference.
Acquire images at six different spots on the culture dish.

steps.title: Quantify scattering intensity in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Analyze confocal images with ImageJ to obtain weighted mean scattering intensity of AuNPs.

substeps.instruction: Open each image in ImageJ (version 1.42q) and select a 512 × 512 pixel region of interest.
Use Analyze → Histogram to generate a list of pixel values and their frequencies.
Determine the background noise threshold from cell‑only (no AuNP) images.
Collect pixel values that are three times greater than the background threshold and compute their average.
Repeat the analysis for five independent confocal images per experimental condition and average the results.

description: We report a simple, rapid, and non-invasive approach for the imaging of sAuNPs within cells by using a standard confocal laser scanning microscope (CLSM). No additional optical or imaging system is required for this approach. A single-wavelength laser excitation was used to excite sAuNPs within the cell, and the reflective images were recorded to explore the size-dependent visibility of the AuNPs. These studies demonstrate that sAuNPs as small as 4 nm in core size can be readily imaged. Image analysis was carried out to explore the correlation between the sAuNP scattering intensity and sAuNP quantities inside cells. Cellular imaging of endosome entrapped small gold nanoparticles was validated using a number of measures.
